name: skeleton-v2-control
question: Does the rebuilt map-town skeleton move the two things the old one could not? The control is assets/raw/_trials/map-fix-round/y6-hearthollow-control.png — the SAME subject at the SAME seed 42 through the OLD skeleton, so exactly one axis moves: the class skeleton. Measure (1) SCALE as the ratio lane-width to building-width, not building width alone, because the known failure mode is the model widening the lane instead of shrinking the buildings; (2) STYLE — does a hard dark keyline appear, are colours flat blocks, is there chequerboard dithering rather than gradient? The old tail crisp clean pixel edges did not hold the idiom and one map came back 99.61% grayscale with no keyline at all. Also watch for regression: y2 showed that adding a scale sentence broke the full-bleed clause standing beside it and put 29% blank void in the frame, so measure void fraction too.

rows.negative: low quality, bad anatomy, extra digits, missing digits, extra limbs, missing limbs
rows.prompt: pixel art isometric town map, retro 90s handheld RPG style, Hearthollow, a farming hamlet of five buildings set well apart around one open grazing green: Warden Maren's timber field station under a shallow plank roof, a fenced specimen pen and drying racks beside it; a stone-walled gym hall under a steep mossy slate roof, its shed and fenced yard at the foot of the green; a long low inn with a byre; a supply shop with a green awning over its door and an open bait crate outside it; and a deep-thatched cottage between a bare fallow field and standing barley; empty cropped turf with nothing built on it at the exact middle of the picture where a worn dirt lane forks, a tall survey board on a post just below the middle; wildflower meadow and a few oaks on the open ground, one thick hedgerow behind the cottage; the lane climbs out through a timber field gate at the top and goes on to the Meadow Reach, Meadow biome, chunky three-quarter isometric view, one single walkable ground level seen from above, the ground plane tilted away from the viewer and every roof, rock and stone standing on it showing one lit top face and two shaded side faces, no characters, the ground named here covers the entire picture and runs off all four sides of it, one continuous piece of that same terrain with no island, no plinth, no cutaway earth wall, no cliff edge, no border and no blank background anywhere, the lane, track or boardwalk running through the town sets the size of everything else, and nothing standing on the ground is wider or taller than that lane is wide, not a building, not a tree, not a rock, the ground between the buildings covered all over with many small things rather than a few large ones, so no stretch of it is left a bare flat field of one colour, every building has one clearly visible door, the walkable ground, the plants, the stone and the timber each keeping their own colour so the ground can be told at a glance from what stands on it, flat blocks of solid colour from a small fixed palette, every shape ringed by a hard dark keyline, regular chequerboard dithering in place of any gradient, every edge a hard pixel step with no blur and no airbrush shading, 2D game asset
